reasoning: Identity, the 25-clause inventory, the quoted spans, the amendment analysis (strike-and-insert items continue as amended, deleted items end on deletion, Sec. 3 executed on signing), the savings statement and the searches are otherwise supported by the held texts, and the FR disposition notes are all addressed. But every structured end date is wrong by three years: whole_order_end and 21 clause first ends give 1971-02-20 for the EO 11768 supersession of February 20, 1974; items (6) and (7) give 1970-07-01 for EO 11727's July 1, 1973 effective date; Section 2 item (8) gives 1970-04-24 for EO 11715 of April 24, 1973; and Section 3 gives 1970-03-23 for the order's own signing on March 23, 1973. Every one of these dates precedes the order's existence and contradicts the claim's own judgment reasons, research rationale and source notes. The claim is internally inconsistent and its dates are wrong, so it must be rejected even though the reasoning reaches the right legal outcome.
